oracle.description: templates/dispatch/tests/test_dispatch_release_stops.py decides correctness. It was written from the M-1 spec row by an author with no access to any implementation, and it is the only judge of this packet.

purpose: Encode the four L-2 stop conditions in the L-1 driver templates/dispatch/scripts/dispatch_release.py. Today the driver stops only when a stage exits non-zero; it has no notion of a stop condition. Add a module constant STOP_CONDITIONS = ("release-boundary", "command-not-allowed", "path-outside-writable", "gate-red-twice") in that order, an optional keyword-only drive() parameter attempts_path: Path | None = None defaulting to worktree.parent / f"{task_id}.attempts.json", and a "stop" key in the report that is None when nothing fired and otherwise a dict carrying at least "condition" (one of STOP_CONDITIONS) and "detail" (a string naming the offending values). Any fired condition must: return a non-zero exit code, write exactly one workflow.escalation through the existing write_escalation path with "stop_condition" in its metadata, and never invoke gh. release-boundary and command-not-allowed have a pre-flight form checked before any stage runs, so report["steps"] is empty; command-not-allowed and path-outside-writable also have a post-gate form checked after the gate stage and before the PR step. gate-red-twice needs a small JSON ledger at attempts_path keyed by starting_commit: the first red gate is recorded and is NOT a stop (existing behaviour survives -- PR skipped with a reason, exit 0), the second red gate on the same packet and starting_commit stops. A gate is red when the gate stage exited non-zero, or its disposition is not "candidate", or its evidence says passed is false. Gate evidence is nested under receipt["evidence"] in a real receipt and flat at the top level in a stubbed one -- read both shapes. Change nothing else in the file: STEPS, the PR command, the never-merge property and the existing report keys all stay exactly as they are.
required_outcomes: STOP_CONDITIONS names the four conditions in the order the spec row lists them
a fired condition exits non-zero, escalates once to workflow.escalation with stop_condition in the metadata, and never opens a PR
release-boundary and an unallowed command id in the packet are caught before any stage runs
an unallowed command id in the gate's command_results and a touched path outside writable_patch_paths are caught after the gate and before the PR
the second red gate on the same packet and starting_commit stops; the first is only recorded
the existing L-1 oracle keeps passing unchanged

acceptance_properties.requirement: the stop-condition vocabulary is fixed and ordered
acceptance_properties.fails_when: STOP_CONDITIONS is absent, is not a tuple, or names the conditions in another order

acceptance_properties.requirement: a release boundary is refused before a worker is ever spent
acceptance_properties.fails_when: release_boundary true runs a stage, exits 0, or fails to escalate

acceptance_properties.requirement: a command id outside allowed_command_ids stops the sequence
acceptance_properties.fails_when: an unallowed id in the packet or in the gate's command_results reaches the PR step

acceptance_properties.requirement: a touched path outside writable_patch_paths stops before the PR
acceptance_properties.fails_when: an out-of-scope touched path is reported as a skipped PR instead of a stop, in either receipt shape

acceptance_properties.requirement: a packet gets one red gate, not two
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the attempt ledger is not written, or a second red gate on the same starting_commit does not stop

acceptance_properties.requirement: the L-1 hand-off contract is unchanged
acceptance_properties.fails_when: any of REQ-001..REQ-005 of the L-1 oracle regresses

non_goals: the L-4 retry policy (that is the next packet)
hybrid_dispatch.py, the packet schema, the manifest or the dispatch policy
